item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate B is substantially closer to the frozen contract because it exposes the exact required Upload signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption usage, and tests retrying streamed file content. Candidate A introduces a conflicting option API and explicitly forbidden association machinery.","reasons":["B implements the required signature exactly: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead accepts ...UploadFileOption.","B directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), as required. A adds NewFileWithFields and routes Upload through that new machinery.","A adds deal, person, organization, product, activity, lead, and project association fields despite the contract explicitly prohibiting association fields.","B keeps existing FilesOption query and request-option behavior for Upload; A invents a parallel option hierarchy that makes the convenience API inconsistent with the established service API and contract wording. B's retry test also uses an os.File and verifies byte-identical multipart bodies across attempts, while A's Upload retry test only uses a strings.Reader and does not compare the complete bodies."],"risks_a":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request/response logic.","The new UploadFileOption API, seven association helpers, multipart field support, retry changes, documentation, and Update commentary create substantial out-of-scope surface area.","No visible Upload test covers propagation of a source-reader failure."],"risks_b":["Upload still calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, violating the contract's centralization requirement and duplicating Add's request/response logic.","It changes generic Raw.Do retry handling for seekable readers even though the contract says not to refactor unrelated retry machinery; seeking to the end also introduces new behavior and possible errors for unusual ReadSeeker implementations.","No visible test covers propagation of a source-reader failure, and the combined validation error is less precise than separate filename/content errors."]}
